His mother reports that he has been generally doing well with no concerns. No family history of cardiovascular disease. The boy does not take any medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since you are a 5-year-old boy with new-onset hypertension and no family history of kidney or adrenal issues, I need to rule out renal causes. Can you show me exactly where your mother feels pain in your stomach or back, or does it hurt anywhere else? REQUEST TEST: Serum_Electrolytes_AND_Creatinine.

speaker: Doctor
text: The blood work shows normal electrolytes and creatinine, which helps rule out obvious renal failure, though the blood pressure remains a concern. Since your family history is negative for kidney or adrenal disease, can you tell me if you have noticed any recent headaches, vision changes, or excessive sweating? REQUEST TEST: Plasma_Aldosterone_TO_Fractalin_Renin_Ratio.

speaker: Doctor
text: The aldosterone-renin ratio is normal, which makes primary hyperaldosteronism unlikely. Since renal parenchymal disease is also ruled out, we need to determine if this is secondary hypertension due to an underlying structural issue. Do you notice any episodes of severe headaches, palpitations, or shaking that might suggest a catecholamine-secreting tumor? REQUEST TEST: Plasma_Catecholamines_and_Metabolites. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_US.

speaker: Doctor
text: The catecholamine levels and abdominal ultrasound are normal, which effectively rules out pheochromocytoma and structural renal abnormalities. Have you noticed any episodes of snoring, gasping for air during sleep, or restless legs? REQUEST TEST: Polysomnography. REQUEST IMAGES: Echocardiogram.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Echocardiogram: Narrowing of the aorta distal to the left subclavian artery with a gradient, consistent with coarctation. Left ventricular function is normal.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Coarctation of the Aorta.

The echocardiogram confirms narrowing of the aorta distal to the left subclavian artery with a gradient, which explains the systemic hypertension. Given your age and the specific location of the obstruction, this is the primary cause of your high blood pressure.
